```{r}
model <- readRDS("../results/multiclass-model.rds")
percent <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * x)

binary_all <- readRDS("../results/binary_final_comparison.rds")
binary_results <- binary_all |> dplyr::filter(variant == "2. more epochs + early stopping")
binary_baseline <- binary_all |> dplyr::filter(variant == "1. baseline (25 units, dropout 0.2, 5 epochs)")
```

### Abstract

**Part (a):** We used paragraph text from each page, represented as TF-IDF word-importance scores, to train a small neural network for binary classification. Training with early stopping to avoid overfitting, the model achieved `r percent(binary_results$accuracy)` validation accuracy. The final model was trained on all 2,165 labeled pages and used to classify 929 test pages.

**Part (b):** We used webpage text to predict five claim categories with ridge multinomial regression. Validation accuracy was `r percent(model$metrics$Accuracy)`. The final model was trained on all 2,165 labeled pages and used to classify 929 test pages.

### Preprocessing

**Part (a):** Paragraph text was extracted from each page's HTML, cleaned (URLs, emails, punctuation, and numbers removed), and converted into TF-IDF scores reflecting how distinctive each word was on that page.

**Part (b):** We extracted titles, headings, and paragraphs, cleaned the text, and converted words and word pairs into TF-IDF scores that reflect their importance in each page.

### Methods

**Part (a):** We trained a small neural network (two dense layers with dropout) on the TF-IDF features. Several alternatives were tested and ruled out: adjusting network size and dropout, a support vector machine, a regularized logistic regression on the full vocabulary, adding page headers/titles to the input text, and tuning the classification threshold. The best and most consistent approach was training with early stopping, which halts training once a held-out validation score stops improving, correcting for overfitting seen with a fixed number of training epochs. The chosen model was evaluated on a held-out 20% test split before being retrained on all labeled data for deployment.

**Part (b):** We fitted ridge multinomial regression, selected its penalty using tuning data, and measured performance on a separate validation set. Pages from the same subject stayed together when splitting the data.

### Results

**Part (a): Binary classification**

```{r}
knitr::kable(data.frame(Model = "Neural network (TF-IDF, early stopping)",
                        Accuracy = percent(binary_results$accuracy),
                        Sensitivity = percent(binary_results$sensitivity),
                        Specificity = percent(binary_results$specificity)))
```

**Part (b): Multiclass classification**

```{r}
knitr::kable(data.frame(Model = "Ridge multinomial regression",
                        Accuracy = percent(model$metrics$Accuracy),
                        Sensitivity = percent(model$metrics$Sensitivity),
                        Specificity = percent(model$metrics$Specificity)))
```

For Part (b), sensitivity and specificity give equal weight to each of the five classes.

### Comparison of models and results

**Part (a):** Accuracy was `r percent(binary_results$accuracy)`, compared with `r percent(binary_baseline$accuracy)` for the same network trained for a fixed 5 epochs without early stopping, which showed signs of memorizing the training data rather than generalizing. None of the alternative methods tested (larger network, higher dropout, SVM, regularized logistic regression, added headers, tuned threshold) outperformed this model on accuracy, though the regularized logistic regression achieved a higher ROC AUC (87.3% vs. 84.2%), suggesting its predicted probabilities ranked pages well even though its default classification cutoff did not.

**Part (b):** Accuracy was `r percent(model$metrics$Accuracy)`, compared with `r percent(model$baseline_accuracy)` for always choosing the most common class. The model identified `r percent(model$per_class$Sensitivity[5])` of “Other claim content” pages, showing room for improvement in this smaller class.

**Overall:** The binary neural network achieved `r percent(binary_results$accuracy)` accuracy, and multiclass ridge regression achieved `r percent(model$metrics$Accuracy)`, with both improving on their own baselines. These accuracies do not directly rank the two methods because the tasks and validation splits differ. A remaining weakness is recognizing “Physical Activity” and “Other claim content” pages, with fewer than half correctly identified in each category. Both models produced predictions for all 929 test pages.
